chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — both together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — regarding

ten (people) who participated jointly in killing a man. He said: 'The family of the killed one has the option: whichever of them they so desire, they may execute (in retaliation), and his guardians have recourse against the remaining ones for nine-tenths of the blood money.'

key_terms.أَعْشَارِ: Tenths — fractions of the full diyah, here nine-tenths owed by the remaining nine perpetrators after one has been executed in qisas
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: Awliya — the legal guardians or next of kin of the victim, who hold the right of qisas and diyah
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diyah — the blood money or financial compensation paid to the victim's family in cases of homicide or bodily harm, a key institution in Islamic criminal law
key_terms.يُخَيَّرُ: Given the choice — the passive verb indicating the victim's family is granted the right to choose which perpetrator to execute

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when multiple people collectively commit a murder according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses a complex case in Islamic criminal law: when a group of people collectively commits a murder, how is justice administered? The ruling establishes that the victim's family retains the right of qisas (retaliatory execution) against any one perpetrator of their choosing, while the remaining perpetrators must collectively pay nine-tenths of the full diyah (blood money). This legal ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential position that collective homicide does not dilute individual accountability, and the victim's family's right of retaliation is preserved while compensatory justice is ensured for the non-executed perpetrators.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding

ten (people) who participated in killing a man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The family of the killed one can choose whichever one they so desire (from the ones who) killed, and his guardians has recourse to the remaining ones for nine-tenths of the wergild’.
